links.outcome: Prompt-injection attack success at primary decision turn across commercial LLMs in simulated medical advice dialogues
links.effect: Attacks achieved 94.4% (102 of 108) success at turn 4 and persisted in 69.4% (75 of 108) of follow-ups; LLM 1 and LLM 2 100% susceptible, LLM 3 83.3%.
links.quote: Across 216 evaluations (108 injection vs 108 control), attacks achieved 94.4% (102 of 108 evaluations) success at turn 4 and persisted in 69.4% (75 of 108 evaluations) of follow-ups.

links.outcome: Vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial injected inputs causing unsafe clinical recommendations, including flagship models
links.effect: Extremely high-harm scenarios (FDA Category X pregnancy drugs) succeeded in 91.7% (33 of 36); flagship models 100% (LLM 4, LLM 5) and 80.0% (LLM 6) vulnerable.
links.quote: The proof-of-concept experiment demonstrated 100% vulnerability for LLM 4 and LLM 5 (5 of 5 dialogues each) and 80.0% (4 of 5 dialogues) for LLM 6.

links.outcome: Undiscovered vulnerabilities to prompt injection and manipulation in commercial LLMs giving medical advice
links.effect: Injection succeeded in 94.4% of evaluations at turn 4; even flagship models showed high susceptibility (80-100%).
links.quote: In this quality improvement study using a controlled simulation, commercial LLMs demonstrated substantial vulnerability to prompt-injection attacks that could generate clinically dangerous recommendations; even flagship models with advanced safety mechanisms showed high susceptibility.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM vulnerabilities to adversarial prompt-injection attacks across clinical scenarios using simulated dialogues, but does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
